q: Dynamical systems and descriptive complexity: the omega-limit set ω(x) of a point x under a continuous map T on a compact space is always:
opts: A closed T-invariant set (non-empty, compact, connected in some cases)
exp: ω(x) = ∩_{n≥0} cl{T^k(x) : k ≥ n} is always non-empty (compactness), closed, and T-invariant. It may not be connected. From a descriptive set theory perspective, the map x ↦ ω(x) (taking values in the hyperspace of closed sets) is Borel measurable but not continuous in general.
